newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to higher ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to higher ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were steady to higher in very quiet trading ahead of the U.S. consumer price data due later on Wednesday, dealers said.
Overnight money was little changed at 5-1/16 4-15/16 percent while three-month money was a touch higher at 5-9/16 7/16 against 5-1/2 3/8 percent on Tuesday.
"There were no trading clues from the U.S. overnight and investors are taking a wait-and-see attitude," a local bank dealer said.
Investors in the local bills and bonds market were taking a defensive position with paper yields edging down between two and three points, a dealer said.
One-week Exchange Fund bills yielded 4.80 percent versus 4.82 percent and three-year notes yielded 6.43 versus 6.46.
The yield on five-year notes was 6.98 versus 7.01 and on seven-year notes 7.35 versus 7.36.
